descriptions.shortDescription: GDPR publication consent management and document metadata enrichment for Nextcloud.
descriptions.longDescription: Filinq provides GDPR-compliant publication consent tracking (Wet Open Overheid) and automatic document metadata enrichment. It integrates with Open Register via events to enrich documents as they are created and updated. Features include consent tracking with configurable objection periods, WOO compliance (minimum 4-week objection period), automatic language detection, keyword extraction, topic classification, PDF generation, document signing (SES/AES/QES), and anonymization. Conduction maintains this component on behalf of the Municipality of Haarlem. Install it from the Nextcloud App Store at https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/filinq.
features: Local processing, no document data leaves your Nextcloud
Detection of names, addresses and BSN numbers before anonymization

descriptions.longDescription: Filinq biedt AVG-conforme bijhouding van publicatietoestemmingen (Wet Open Overheid) en automatische verrijking van documentmetadata. Het integreert via events met Open Register om documenten te verrijken zodra ze worden aangemaakt of bijgewerkt. Functionaliteit omvat toestemmingsbeheer met instelbare bezwaarperiodes, WOO-compliance (minimaal 4 weken bezwaartermijn), automatische taaldetectie, trefwoordextractie, onderwerpclassificatie, PDF-generatie, documentondertekening (SES/AES/QES) en anonimisering. Conduction onderhoudt dit component in opdracht van Gemeente Haarlem. Installeer het vanuit de Nextcloud App Store op https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/filinq.
features: Lokale verwerking, er verlaat geen documentdata je Nextcloud
Herkenning van namen, adressen en BSN-nummers voor anonimisering

sources.subject: ConductionNL/filinq
sources.caveat: Authors of the latest 1000 commits of the last 12 months, told apart by address after the repository's .mailmap. Their organisation is the domain of their address, or for a personal, hidden or noreply address the company on their public profile. The owning organisation (conduction.nl) is the most common organisation domain, the domains and names in publiccode.yml and the owner account; one person with two addresses counts twice. Bots are left out.

results.title: Project health (CHAOSS)
results.description: How active and widely carried the project is: the bus factor, the spread over organisations, how change requests and issues are handled, and how often it releases. Informative: shown, not rated.
results.message: 6 of 6 CHAOSS metrics measured. They are shown for information and do not count in any rating.

metrics.name: Contributor Absence Factor
metrics.explanation: The fewest people who together made half of the commits on the default branch in the last 12 months, of the 100 contributors GitHub reports, among 9 human contributors. At 1 the project depends on a single person. Bots are left out; one person with several accounts or addresses counts more than once.

metrics.name: Organizational Diversity
metrics.explanation: Organisations are told apart by the email domain of the latest 300 commits of the last 12 months (194 commits by people, after the .mailmap) and, for a personal or hidden address, by the company on the author's public profile. The largest is conduction.nl (3 authors), with 100% of the 194 commits whose organisation is known; 0% of the commits come from 0 of 3 authors whose organisation stays unknown. Only these counts are kept, no names, addresses or companies; an organisation is named only when several authors share it.

metrics.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
metrics.explanation: 1,377 change requests were closed (merged or not) and 1,399 opened in the last 90 days, bots included. Below 1 the open backlog grows; above 1 it shrinks.

metrics.name: Time to First Response
metrics.explanation: None of the 15 latest change requests opened by people between 2026-08-27 and 2026-11-18 got a comment or review from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Issue Response Time
metrics.explanation: None of the 4 latest issues opened by people between 2026-08-27 and 2026-11-18 got a comment from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Release Frequency
metrics.explanation: 7 final releases were published in the last 12 months, about one every 52 days, counted from the GitHub releases. The latest final release is from 2026-09-06. Besides these, 509 pre-releases were published; they are not counted. Drafts and pre-releases are left out.

openBreaches.title: [CRITICAL] Signature verification always returns valid — no cryptographic check
[HIGH] Detected numeric PII silently skipped by anonymization
[HIGH] Anonymization reports a replacement count that may be fabricated
[MEDIUM] NativeSigningProvider sessions in-memory only — signing flow cannot complete
[MEDIUM] Broad Throwable fallback in listRequests masks real failures as empty success
[MEDIUM] Audit immutability not enforced at storage layer — Archiefwet compliance gap
[LOW] Deep-review minor findings: audit memory load and consent extra fields
Lint debt cleanup post-canonical-sync (Phase 2 fleet rollout)

notes: Measured over the open issues and the issues closed in the last 90 days, in working days (Monday to Friday, Europe/Amsterdam, without Dutch public holidays).
Only the 200 most recently updated issues of each kind were read.

Vulnerabilities are read from the published GitHub security advisories, from draft to publication. Their response time, unpublished advisories and Dependabot alerts need admin rights and are not measured.
2 of 301 issues were opened by the maintainers themselves; they have a fix term but no response term.
No issue carries a blocking label (such as blocker or critical), so every bug counts as an other bug.
